# Best rechargeable AA batteries

**Best overall: Panasonic Eneloop Pro AA (NiMH, ~2,550 mAh).** Digital Camera World's reviewer picked it as best overall after years of using it in flashes, with no reliability problems. It's pre-charged, keeps about 85% of its charge after a year, and works from -20 to 50 °C. The tradeoff is a rating of only about 500 recharge cycles, and it costs more than the alternatives. GearLab also names it best overall for high-drain devices like cameras and controllers.
- Where to buy: retailer links (Adorama, Amazon, Newegg, Best Buy) are in the [Digital Camera World guide](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries). It lists prices from about $22 to $35, though it doesn't say what pack size those are for.

**Best for lots of recharges: standard Panasonic Eneloop AA (~2,000 mAh).** It has lower capacity, so each charge is shorter, but it is rated for about 2,100 recharges. It's a better pick for devices you recharge constantly. Buy links are in the [same guide](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries).

**Best budget, if you're near an IKEA: LADDA.** Charge-Test's lab measurements found the LADDA 2450 mAh cells trade blows with Eneloop Pro. They averaged about 2,450 mAh at low load and about 2,350 mAh at 1 A. Its verdict was that LADDA is "Eneloop-class cells at budget prices," though IKEA has never confirmed Panasonic makes them ([Charge-Test review](https://charge-test.com/ikea-ladda-batteries-review-still-the-best-budget-aa-aaa-rechargeable-in-2026/)).
- The US IKEA page I could see lists only the **1900 mAh** model at $9.99 for 4 ([IKEA LADDA AA 1900 mAh](https://www.ikea.com/us/en/p/ladda-rechargeable-battery-hr06-aa-1-2v-00509814/)). Its reviews are strong (4.7 of 5 across 1,009 reviews).
- GearLab says the 2450 model is $7.99 in-store, but I couldn't confirm that on IKEA's US site. Check availability at your local store first.

**Best for bulk or high capacity: Tenergy Premium PRO AA (2,800 mAh), 20-pack for $42.99.** That works out to about $2.15 per cell, and the same listing also sells 4-, 8- and 12-packs. Tenergy rates it at 1,200 cycles and 85% charge retained after a year. These figures come from the manufacturer, not independent testing. The warranty is also unclear: the product page says 12 months, but Tenergy's warranty page says 90 days. Returns are 30 days, and you pay return shipping.
- [Buy the Tenergy 20-pack](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-premium-pro-aa-2800mah-20-pack). This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you.

**Best for devices that need 1.5 V: EBL 1.5V Li-ion AA.** Digital Camera World recommends these for voltage-sensitive devices that don't like the 1.2 V of NiMH cells. Buy links are in the [guide](https://www.digitalcameraworld.com/buying-guides/best-rechargeable-aa-batteries).

## Caveats
- **Amazon Basics High-Capacity:** Frame & Focal's tests found it lost the most capacity under heavy load and over a year of use ([12-month test](https://frameandfocal.com/camera-reviews/which-aa-rechargeable-battery-best-after-one-year-abuse-440920)). GearLab suggests it only for low-drain devices like remotes and clocks ([GearLab](https://gearlab.io/best-rechargeable-batteries-for-household-devices/)). I'd skip it for cameras, flashes or flashlights.
- **Frame & Focal's data:** parts of it look inconsistent (for example, Eneloop Pro capacity figures that don't match Panasonic's rating). I'd trust its overall ranking more than its exact numbers.
- **Chargers:** the cells are only as good as the charger. A smart charger that handles each cell individually is worth having. IKEA's STENKOL charger is $8.99.

**My pick:** Eneloop Pro if you want the proven choice for high-drain gear. LADDA 2450 if you can get it at IKEA for less. The Tenergy 20-pack if you need a lot of cells at once.
